g.text: Day 7 block — 4 memory types, where data lives, when to use which
The problem — your agent has amnesia
User (Mon): My name is Priya and I'm learning Python.
Agent: Hi Priya! Happy to help with Python.
User (Fri, new session): What was I learning again?
Agent: I don't know. Who are you?
Every LLM call is stateless. The model forgets
the second you close the terminal.
Memory = relevant past data + injected into the next prompt
The LLM never 'remembers'. YOUR CODE fetches past data
and shows it to the LLM each turn.
4 memory types — borrowed from your own brain
Working — what you're thinking right now
Episodic — that one time at the hostel
Procedural — how to ride a bike
Every production AI agent uses some mix of these 4. Learn the mapping.
a Python list, Redis, or session_state
appended to messages[] on every call
The easiest memory. The chatbot you built on Day 3 already had this.
fetched by user_id at session start, summarized into system prompt
summaries lose detail, old chats pile up
store full chat + a summary; retrieve only summaries
This is why ChatGPT 'remembers' you across sessions.
3. Semantic memory — facts about the user and the world
top-K most relevant facts, selected by query embedding
forever, but editable (user: 'I'm not vegetarian anymore')
wrong facts get sticky — version them
The 'memory' most AI products are shipping in 2026.
JSON/YAML files, or a workflow store
a few-shot example or a cached tool-call sequence
as long as the API doesn't change
brittle — upstream API change breaks the stored workflow
rare in B.Tech projects; common in production copilots
Advanced. Know it exists. We won't build it today.
in-memory Python list — lost on restart
JSON on disk — survives restart, single machine
Pick the lowest layer that solves your problem.
4 types, one prompt-build function. That's the whole trick.
In production, you'll likely use one of these. Build from scratch once
Decision tree — pick a memory for your project
Most useful agents end up with Working + Semantic. That's today's project.
User changed jobs 2 years ago, memory still says 'student'.
User's old password mentioned in chat, now stored forever.
Memory makes agents feel human. It also makes them liable.
Hands-on — a memory lab with all 4 types
Boot it up, chat, break it, inspect the files.
• 4 memory types mapped to the human brain
• A working agent that remembers across sessions
• You'll see data appear in SQLite, Chroma, JSON — live
• You'll know when to swap custom code for mem0 in production
Memory is what turns a chatbot into a companion. Build it, see it, break it.
